This is goal g-33a7a4ae, round 2 (fix round; round 1 was audit-only and already merged as docs/state/silent-failures.md; a first fix batch for tools/gc.mjs, tools/ledger-backup.mjs, tools/autopilot.mjs already merged). Read that doc's methodology section first (top of file) and the two per-file sections for tools/board-data.mjs and tools/board.mjs (search for '### tools/board-data.mjs' and '### tools/board.mjs' - each lists exact line numbers and the catch form found there: try-catch-no-binding, dot-catch-arrow, or dot-catch-noop-expr).

For EACH flagged line in those two files only (do not touch any other file, do not fix findings in other files even if you notice them while reading):

1. Read the surrounding function to understand what the catch is actually guarding against and what happens today when it swallows silently (what does the function return/do next).
2. Decide, from the real code, whether this catch is:
   (a) An EXPECTED/benign condition already evidenced by context - e.g. an optional file that may not exist yet (ENOENT), a best-effort read of board/project state that may not exist on first run, a value that legitimately may be missing. For these, keep the swallow (do not change control flow or add noisy logging for the expected path), but if the catch currently swallows ANY error unconditionally, narrow it: check the error's code/message for the specific expected case (e.g. `error?.code === 'ENOENT'`) and continue silently only for that case; for anything else unexpected, add minimal visibility (see point 3) before continuing with the SAME behavior as today (still no throw, same return value) - the goal is 'stop eating unrelated bugs disguised as the expected case', not changing what the function returns.
   (b) A genuinely UNEXPECTED-error catch with no narrower expected case. Add minimal visibility only: a one-line log of the error's message. These two files have no existing logger/journal convention of their own (checked) - use `console.error('[tools/<file>.mjs] <short context naming the function/operation>:', error?.message ?? error)`. Do NOT add a throw, do NOT change the function's return value or control flow, do NOT change what happens next - this is a visibility-only fix, not a behavior change.
3. If a catch binds no error variable (`catch {}` / `catch { ... }` / `.catch(() => {})` / `.catch(() => undefined)`), add a REAL binding (`catch (error) { ... }` / `.catch((error) => { ... })`) and actually reference it in a console.error call - do not just rename-and-ignore it (e.g. `catch (error) { error; }` is not an acceptable fix; it must either narrow by error code with a real log for the unexpected branch, or log unconditionally).

Do not refactor anything beyond the flagged catch blocks. Do not reformat unrelated code. Do not rename functions or change exports. Preserve every existing behavior path exactly except for the narrowing/visibility described above.

Your workspace does not include the test suite, so you cannot run it yourself - the orchestrator runs the real full suite against your output after integration and will send back any regression as a follow-up. List, in your final summary, which of the 32 flagged lines you narrowed (case a) vs. just added logging to (case b), with one line each.
